# Countdown

A ticking countdown that shows only the units it needs.

- Category: Data & feedback
- Widgets: `CairnCountdown`, `CairnCountdownDigits`, `CairnCountdownDigits`
- Import: `import 'package:cairn_ui/cairn_ui.dart';`

> Owns a Timer that ticks once a second. Remove it from the tree to dispose it.

## Quick start

```dart
CairnCountdown(
  duration: const Duration(hours: 26, minutes: 14),
  onComplete: _launch,
)
```

## Variants and examples

### Days and hours

```dart
const CairnCountdown(duration: Duration(hours: 26, minutes: 14))
```

### Minutes only

```dart
const CairnCountdown(duration: Duration(minutes: 5))
```

## API

### `CairnCountdown` (widget)

A ticking countdown to zero, shown as labelled digit blocks.

Counts down from [duration] once per second, rendering days (only when the
duration reaches that far), hours, minutes and seconds as two-digit blocks
in tabular figures so the layout does not jitter as digits change. Each
block is a `muted` rounded tile with a small caption beneath it.

[onComplete] fires once, when the count reaches zero. Changing [duration]
restarts the countdown.

For a bare digit with no tile — a single number inside a sentence — use
[CairnCountdownDigits].

```dart
CairnCountdown(
  duration: const Duration(hours: 2, minutes: 30),
  onComplete: () => print('Sale over'),
);
```

**Constructor** `CairnCountdown({required Duration duration, VoidCallback? onComplete})`

Creates a countdown.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `duration` | `Duration` | yes |  | How long to count down for. |
| `onComplete` | `VoidCallback?` |  |  | Called once when the countdown reaches zero. |

### `CairnCountdownDigits` (widget)

A number rendered as zero-padded, tabular digits.

Tabular figures give every digit the same advance, so a ticking value does
not shift the text around it. Inherits its style from the ambient
[DefaultTextStyle] unless [style] is given.

**Constructor** `CairnCountdownDigits({required int value, int minDigits = 2, TextStyle? style})`

Creates a digit run.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `value` | `int` | yes |  | The number to show. |
| `minDigits` | `int` |  | `2` | The minimum width, zero-padded. |
| `style` | `TextStyle?` |  |  | The text style. |


---

# Design tokens

## `CairnTheme` (widget)

The design tokens every Cairn component reads from.

`CairnTheme` is a [ThemeExtension], which is the deliberate integration
choice for this library. The alternative — an inherited widget of Cairn's
own — would have forced host apps to nest two theme systems and would have
broken any Material widget they already use. Riding on
[ThemeData.extensions] instead means:

* Cairn composes inside an ordinary [MaterialApp]; nothing has to be
  abandoned or wrapped.
* Flutter animates theme changes for free, because [ThemeExtension.lerp] is
  driven by [AnimatedTheme] during a light/dark transition.
* `Theme.of(context)` stays the single lookup path developers already know.

## Usage

The direct form:

```dart
MaterialApp(
  theme: ThemeData(extensions: const <ThemeExtension<dynamic>>[CairnTheme.light]),
  darkTheme: ThemeData(extensions: const <ThemeExtension<dynamic>>[CairnTheme.dark]),
);
```

Or let [CairnTheme.materialTheme] build a [ThemeData] whose Material
defaults (scaffold background, text selection, splash behaviour) already
agree with the Cairn tokens:

```dart
MaterialApp(
  theme: CairnTheme.materialTheme(CairnTheme.light),
  darkTheme: CairnTheme.materialTheme(CairnTheme.dark),
);
```

Components resolve tokens with [CairnTheme.of], which falls back to
[CairnTheme.light] rather than throwing, so a widget dropped into an app
with no extension registered still renders correctly.

**Constructor** `CairnTheme({required Brightness brightness, required Color background, required Color foreground, required Color card, required Color cardForeground, required Color popover, required Color popoverForeground, required Color primary, required Color primaryForeground, required Color secondary, required Color secondaryForeground, required Color muted, required Color mutedForeground, required Color accent, required Color accentForeground, required Color destructive, required Color destructiveForeground, required Color border, required Color input, required Color ring, double radius = CairnRadius.base, String? fontFamily, List<String>? fontFamilyFallback})`

Creates a theme from an explicit set of tokens.

Prefer [CairnTheme.light] / [CairnTheme.dark] and [copyWith] for
customisation; this constructor exists for themes built from scratch.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `brightness` | `Brightness` | yes |  | Whether this is a light or dark theme. A handful of components genuinely branch on brightness rather than on a token, because the dark theme asks for a treatment with no light-mode counterpart. The outline Button is the clearest case: on a dark page a hairline border alone barely separates the control from its background, so it takes a faint fill that would be redundant in light mode. |
| `background` | `Color` | yes |  | The page surface. |
| `foreground` | `Color` | yes |  | Default body text on [background]. |
| `card` | `Color` | yes |  | Raised content surfaces. |
| `cardForeground` | `Color` | yes |  | Text on [card]. |
| `popover` | `Color` | yes |  | Floating surfaces: Popover, Dropdown Menu, Select, Tooltip bodies, Command palette. |
| `popoverForeground` | `Color` | yes |  | Text on [popover]. |
| `primary` | `Color` | yes |  | High-emphasis fills — the default Button, the checked Checkbox and Switch, the Progress indicator. |
| `primaryForeground` | `Color` | yes |  | Text and icons on [primary]. |
| `secondary` | `Color` | yes |  | Low-emphasis fills — the secondary Button and Badge. |
| `secondaryForeground` | `Color` | yes |  | Text on [secondary]. |
| `muted` | `Color` | yes |  | De-emphasised backgrounds — Slider track, Table footer. |
| `mutedForeground` | `Color` | yes |  | Secondary text — descriptions, placeholders. |
| `accent` | `Color` | yes |  | Hover and keyboard-focus highlight for interactive rows. |
| `accentForeground` | `Color` | yes |  | Text on [accent]. |
| `destructive` | `Color` | yes |  | Danger fills and destructive text. |
| `destructiveForeground` | `Color` | yes |  | The foreground paired with [destructive] fills. A slot of its own rather than a hardcoded white, so a theme that softens the destructive fill can move the text sitting on it as well. |
| `border` | `Color` | yes |  | Hairlines and component outlines. |
| `input` | `Color` | yes |  | The border color of form controls specifically. Tokenised separately from [border] so that inputs can read at a different weight from ordinary hairlines — which the dark theme uses, lifting form controls to 15% white where a plain border sits at 10%. |
| `ring` | `Color` | yes |  | The focus ring color. Components draw it at 50% alpha and 3px thickness; see [focusRing]. |
| `radius` | `double` |  | `CairnRadius.base` | The base corner radius, in logical pixels. Defaults to [CairnRadius.base] (10.0). Change this to rescale every component's corners proportionally; see [radiusScale]. |
| `fontFamily` | `String?` |  |  | The font family applied to all Cairn text. Null means "inherit whatever the host app set". Cairn names no typeface of its own, so it adopts the host's rather than imposing one. |
| `fontFamilyFallback` | `List<String>?` |  |  | Fallback families for [fontFamily]. |

**Static members**

- `CairnTheme light = CairnTheme(brightness: Brightness.light, background: CairnColors.lightBackground, foreground: CairnColors.lightForeground, card: CairnColors.lightCard, cardF...` — Cairn's default light theme.
- `CairnTheme dark = CairnTheme(brightness: Brightness.dark, background: CairnColors.darkBackground, foreground: CairnColors.darkForeground, card: CairnColors.darkCard, cardForeg...` — Cairn's default dark theme.
- `CairnTheme of(BuildContext context)` — Resolves the ambient theme, falling back to [CairnTheme.light]. The fallback is intentional: a Cairn widget used in an app that never registered the extension still renders with correct tokens instead of throwing. Register the extension to control which theme is used.
- `ThemeData materialTheme(CairnTheme cairn)` — Builds a [ThemeData] whose Material defaults agree with [cairn]. This does not replace Material — it aligns it, so a host app mixing Cairn widgets with Material ones does not get two clashing palettes. It sets the scaffold and canvas colors, a matching [ColorScheme], the text selection colors, and disables Material's ink splash (Cairn has no ripple; its interactions are colour and shadow transitions only).
- `double lerpDouble(double a, double b, double t)` — Linearly interpolates two non-null doubles.

**Members**

- `CairnRadiusScale get radiusScale` — The derived radius scale for this theme's [radius].
- `Color get ringMuted` — [ring] at the 50% alpha the focus ring is drawn with.
- `Color get overlay` — The scrim behind modal surfaces — black at 50%.
- `List<BoxShadow> get focusRing` — The focus ring as a box-shadow list. Tailwind implements `ring-[3px]` as `box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px <color>` — a hard, unblurred outset. The Flutter equivalent is a [BoxShadow] with zero offset, zero blur and a 3px spread, which is what this returns.
- `List<BoxShadow> get invalidRing` — The focus ring tinted for invalid controls. [destructive] at 20% alpha, raised to 40% in the dark theme where the lower-contrast surface needs the extra weight to register.
- `TextStyle textStyle(TextStyle base)` — Applies [fontFamily] and [fontFamilyFallback] to a token text style.
- `TextStyle get defaultTextStyle` — The default text style for this theme: `text-sm` in [foreground].

## `CairnColors`

Cairn's semantic color tokens, as Flutter [Color] constants.

## How the palette is built

Cairn ships one neutral base palette in two themes. Every value is authored
in the CSS `oklch()` color function rather than as hex, because OKLCH is
perceptually uniform: the light and dark themes are two readings of the same
lightness ramp, so a pair that is legible in one is legible in the other by
construction rather than by eye. Each constant below records the literal
`oklch()` string it was authored as, and `test/tokens/colors_test.dart`
re-derives every constant through [Oklch.toColor] to prove the baked value
still matches that source.

The achromatic steps land exactly on Tailwind's published `neutral` ramp —
`oklch(0.145 0 0)` is `#0A0A0A` (neutral-950), `oklch(0.922 0 0)` is
`#E5E5E5` (neutral-200). That is both an independent check that the OKLab
pipeline is correct and a convenience: Cairn's greys sit flush against a
Tailwind-flavoured design without a seam.

## Roles, not shades

Tokens are named for the job they do — `primary`, `mutedForeground`,
`border` — never for how they look. A component asks for *the foreground
that belongs on a destructive surface*, not for white, which is what makes
overriding a single slot in [CairnTheme] re-theme every component that
reads it.

These raw constants are rarely used directly; consume them through
[CairnTheme], which exposes the same slots and supports overriding.

**Static members**

- `Color lightBackground = Color(0xFFFFFFFF)` — `background` = `oklch(1 0 0)` — `#FFFFFF`.
- `Color lightForeground = Color(0xFF0A0A0A)` — `foreground` = `oklch(0.145 0 0)` — `#0A0A0A` (neutral-950).
- `Color lightCard = Color(0xFFFFFFFF)` — `card` = `oklch(1 0 0)` — `#FFFFFF`.
- `Color lightCardForeground = Color(0xFF0A0A0A)` — `cardForeground` = `oklch(0.145 0 0)` — `#0A0A0A`.
- `Color lightPopover = Color(0xFFFFFFFF)` — `popover` = `oklch(1 0 0)` — `#FFFFFF`.
- `Color lightPopoverForeground = Color(0xFF0A0A0A)` — `popoverForeground` = `oklch(0.145 0 0)` — `#0A0A0A`.
- `Color lightPrimary = Color(0xFF171717)` — `primary` = `oklch(0.205 0 0)` — `#171717` (neutral-900).
- `Color lightPrimaryForeground = Color(0xFFFAFAFA)` — `primaryForeground` = `oklch(0.985 0 0)` — `#FAFAFA` (neutral-50).
- `Color lightSecondary = Color(0xFFF5F5F5)` — `secondary` = `oklch(0.97 0 0)` — `#F5F5F5` (neutral-100).
- `Color lightSecondaryForeground = Color(0xFF171717)` — `secondaryForeground` = `oklch(0.205 0 0)` — `#171717`.
- `Color lightMuted = Color(0xFFF5F5F5)` — `muted` = `oklch(0.97 0 0)` — `#F5F5F5`.
- `Color lightMutedForeground = Color(0xFF737373)` — `mutedForeground` = `oklch(0.556 0 0)` — `#737373` (neutral-500).
- `Color lightAccent = Color(0xFFF5F5F5)` — `accent` = `oklch(0.97 0 0)` — `#F5F5F5`.
- `Color lightAccentForeground = Color(0xFF171717)` — `accentForeground` = `oklch(0.205 0 0)` — `#171717`.
- `Color lightDestructive = Color(0xFFE7000B)` — `destructive` = `oklch(0.577 0.245 27.325)` — `#E7000B` (red-600).
- `Color lightDestructiveForeground = Color(0xFFFFFFFF)` — The foreground that sits on destructive surfaces. Kept as its own slot rather than hardcoding white into destructive Buttons and Badges: a theme that softens the destructive fill needs to move the text on it too, and a hardcoded colour would leave that unreachable. The default is white, which is what the default red needs.
- `Color lightBorder = Color(0xFFE5E5E5)` — `border` = `oklch(0.922 0 0)` — `#E5E5E5` (neutral-200).
- `Color lightInput = Color(0xFFE5E5E5)` — `input` = `oklch(0.922 0 0)` — `#E5E5E5`.
- `Color lightRing = Color(0xFFA1A1A1)` — `ring` = `oklch(0.708 0 0)` — `#A1A1A1` (neutral-400).
- `Color darkBackground = Color(0xFF0A0A0A)` — `background` = `oklch(0.145 0 0)` — `#0A0A0A`.
- `Color darkForeground = Color(0xFFFAFAFA)` — `foreground` = `oklch(0.985 0 0)` — `#FAFAFA`.
- `Color darkCard = Color(0xFF171717)` — `card` = `oklch(0.205 0 0)` — `#171717`. Dark cards sit *lighter* than the page, inverting the light theme's relationship where the card is white on a near-white page.
- `Color darkCardForeground = Color(0xFFFAFAFA)` — `cardForeground` = `oklch(0.985 0 0)` — `#FAFAFA`.
- `Color darkPopover = Color(0xFF171717)` — `popover` = `oklch(0.205 0 0)` — `#171717`.
- `Color darkPopoverForeground = Color(0xFFFAFAFA)` — `popoverForeground` = `oklch(0.985 0 0)` — `#FAFAFA`.
- `Color darkPrimary = Color(0xFFE5E5E5)` — `primary` = `oklch(0.922 0 0)` — `#E5E5E5` (neutral-200).
- `Color darkPrimaryForeground = Color(0xFF171717)` — `primaryForeground` = `oklch(0.205 0 0)` — `#171717`.
- `Color darkSecondary = Color(0xFF262626)` — `secondary` = `oklch(0.269 0 0)` — `#262626` (neutral-800).
- `Color darkSecondaryForeground = Color(0xFFFAFAFA)` — `secondaryForeground` = `oklch(0.985 0 0)` — `#FAFAFA`.
- `Color darkMuted = Color(0xFF262626)` — `muted` = `oklch(0.269 0 0)` — `#262626`.
- `Color darkMutedForeground = Color(0xFFA1A1A1)` — `mutedForeground` = `oklch(0.708 0 0)` — `#A1A1A1`.
- `Color darkAccent = Color(0xFF262626)` — `accent` = `oklch(0.269 0 0)` — `#262626`.
- `Color darkAccentForeground = Color(0xFFFAFAFA)` — `accentForeground` = `oklch(0.985 0 0)` — `#FAFAFA`.
- `Color darkDestructive = Color(0xFFFF6467)` — `destructive` = `oklch(0.704 0.191 22.216)` — `#FF6467` (red-400).
- `Color darkDestructiveForeground = Color(0xFFFFFFFF)` — White. The destructive fill stays saturated in the dark theme, so the foreground pairing does not change between themes.
- `Color darkBorder = Color(0x1AFFFFFF)` — `border` = `oklch(1 0 0 / 10%)` — white at 10% alpha. The dark theme switches borders from an opaque grey to a translucent white so they lift correctly over both the page and raised card surfaces.
- `Color darkInput = Color(0x26FFFFFF)` — `input` = `oklch(1 0 0 / 15%)` — white at 15% alpha.
- `Color darkRing = Color(0xFF737373)` — `ring` = `oklch(0.556 0 0)` — `#737373`.
- `Color chart1 = Color(0xFFD4D4D4)` — `chart1` = `oklch(0.87 0 0)` — `#D4D4D4`.
- `Color chart2 = Color(0xFF737373)` — `chart2` = `oklch(0.556 0 0)` — `#737373`.
- `Color chart3 = Color(0xFF525252)` — `chart3` = `oklch(0.439 0 0)` — `#525252`.
- `Color chart4 = Color(0xFF404040)` — `chart4` = `oklch(0.371 0 0)` — `#404040`.
- `Color chart5 = Color(0xFF262626)` — `chart5` = `oklch(0.269 0 0)` — `#262626`.
- `Color overlay = Color(0x80000000)` — The scrim behind Dialog, Alert Dialog, Sheet and Drawer. Black at 50%, and deliberately not a theme slot: a scrim's job is to darken whatever happens to be behind it, which is the same job in both themes.
- `Color white = Color(0xFFFFFFFF)` — Pure white, for text on destructive fills and for the Slider thumb, which stays white in both themes.

## `CairnMotion`

Cairn's transition durations and easing curves.

The default is `150ms` on a `cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)` curve — an
asymmetric ease that leaves quickly and arrives slowly, which is what makes
a hover or press state feel responsive rather than sluggish. Note that this
is *not* the CSS keyword `ease-in-out` (`cubic-bezier(0.42, 0, 0.58, 1)`),
which is symmetric and reads as noticeably lazier on short transitions.

Individual components override the duration where the distance travelled
justifies it: Dialog and Alert Dialog use 200ms, Accordion animates its
height over 200ms, and Sheet is deliberately asymmetric — 500ms to open,
300ms to close.

Flutter ships no built-in [Curve] with those control points, so [standard]
constructs one with [Cubic].

**Static members**

- `Duration d75 = Duration(milliseconds: 75)` — `duration-75`.
- `Duration d100 = Duration(milliseconds: 100)` — `duration-100`.
- `Duration d150 = Duration(milliseconds: 150)` — `duration-150` — Tailwind's `transition` default.
- `Duration d200 = Duration(milliseconds: 200)` — `duration-200` — Dialog, Alert Dialog, Accordion, Popover.
- `Duration d300 = Duration(milliseconds: 300)` — `duration-300` — Sheet and Drawer closing.
- `Duration d500 = Duration(milliseconds: 500)` — `duration-500` — Sheet and Drawer opening.
- `Duration d1000 = Duration(milliseconds: 1000)` — `duration-1000` — the Input OTP caret blink.
- `Cubic standard = Cubic(0.4, 0.0, 0.2, 1.0)` — Tailwind's default easing, `cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)`. Applied to colour, shadow and transform transitions across the library. Identical in value to Flutter's [Curves.fastOutSlowIn]'s intent but spelled out so the provenance is unambiguous.
- `Cubic easeOut = Cubic(0.0, 0.0, 0.2, 1.0)` — `ease-out` — `cubic-bezier(0, 0, 0.2, 1)`. Entrance transitions.
- `Cubic easeIn = Cubic(0.4, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0)` — `ease-in` — `cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 1, 1)`. Exit transitions.
- `Curve linear = Curves.linear` — `linear` — used by the Spinner and the indeterminate Progress sweep.
- `Duration pulse = Duration(seconds: 2)` — The `animate-pulse` keyframe duration used by Skeleton (`2s`).
- `Duration spin = Duration(seconds: 1)` — The `animate-spin` rotation period used by Spinner (`1s`).

## `Oklch`

Converts colors expressed in the CSS `oklch()` color function into
Flutter [Color] values.

Cairn's palette is authored in OKLCH rather than HSL or raw hex. OKLCH is
perceptually uniform: an equal step in `L` reads as an equal step in
brightness at every hue, which is what keeps a light and a dark theme
derived from the same ramp visually balanced. Every semantic color token in
[CairnColors] is therefore written as an `oklch()` triple and converted
here.

Keeping the conversion in the package (rather than pasting pre-computed hex
values) means the provenance of every color is checkable: the doc comment on
each token records the literal `oklch()` string it was authored as, and
`test/tokens/oklch_test.dart` re-derives the baked constants from it.

The pipeline is the standard one from Björn Ottosson's OKLab specification:

```text
OKLCH -> OKLab -> LMS' -> LMS -> linear sRGB -> gamma-encoded sRGB
```

Out-of-gamut results are clipped per channel, which matches how browsers
render these particular tokens (all of Cairn's default tokens are in-gamut
for sRGB, so clipping is a safety net rather than a routine operation).

**Static members**

- `Color toColor(double l, double c, double h, {double opacity = 1.0})` — Converts an `oklch(L C H)` triple to a [Color]. [l] is perceptual lightness in the range 0..1, [c] is chroma (0 for the achromatic greys that make up most of Cairn's neutral base), and [h] is the hue angle in degrees. [opacity] maps to the `/ <alpha>` component of the CSS function and defaults to fully opaque. ```dart // --background: oklch(1 0 0)  ->  #FFFFFF Oklch.toColor(1, 0, 0); ```

## `CairnRadius`

Cairn's border-radius scale, expressed in Flutter logical pixels.

The entire scale derives from a single base value, [base], which defaults to
10 logical pixels. Every step is a fixed **multiple** of that base:

```text
xs  = 2 (fixed)
sm  = base * 0.6   ->  6
md  = base * 0.8   ->  8
lg  = base         -> 10
xl  = base * 1.4   -> 14
2xl = base * 1.8   -> 18
3xl = base * 2.2   -> 22
4xl = base * 2.6   -> 26
```

Multipliers rather than offsets is a deliberate choice. The obvious
alternative — fixed pixel offsets from the base (`base - 4`, `base - 2`,
`base + 4`) — produces identical numbers at the default base, but falls
apart the moment the base is retuned: a compact 4px theme would give a
*negative* small radius, and a generous 24px theme would compress the whole
scale into a narrow band. A proportional scale holds its shape at any base,
so changing `CairnTheme.radius` rescales every corner in the library
coherently instead of requiring a per-component audit. [CairnRadius.scaled]
is that computation.

**Static members**

- `double base = 10.0` — The base radius: 10 logical pixels.
- `double none = 0.0` — No rounding — 0px.
- `double xs = 2.0` — 2px. A fixed step rather than a multiple of [base]. Used by the close-button affordance in Dialog and Sheet, where the target is small enough that a proportional radius would read as a circle.
- `double sm = 6.0` — `base * 0.6` = 6px.
- `double md = 8.0` — `base * 0.8` = 8px. The most common radius in the library: Button, Input, Textarea, Select trigger, Popover and Dropdown content all use it.
- `double lg = 10.0` — `base` = 10px. Used by Dialog, Alert and Tabs list.
- `double xl = 14.0` — `base * 1.4` = 14px. Used by Card.
- `double xl2 = 18.0` — `base * 1.8` = 18px.
- `double xl3 = 22.0` — `base * 2.2` = 22px.
- `double xl4 = 26.0` — `base * 2.6` = 26px.
- `double full = 9999.0` — A very large radius that reads as a pill or circle. CSS uses `9999px`; Flutter clamps a [BorderRadius] to half the shorter side, so any sufficiently large number behaves identically.
- `BorderRadius brSm = BorderRadius.all(Radius.circular(sm))` — `BorderRadius.circular(CairnRadius.sm)`.
- `BorderRadius brMd = BorderRadius.all(Radius.circular(md))` — `BorderRadius.circular(CairnRadius.md)`.
- `BorderRadius brLg = BorderRadius.all(Radius.circular(lg))` — `BorderRadius.circular(CairnRadius.lg)`.
- `BorderRadius brXl = BorderRadius.all(Radius.circular(xl))` — `BorderRadius.circular(CairnRadius.xl)`.
- `BorderRadius brFull = BorderRadius.all(Radius.circular(full))` — `BorderRadius.circular(CairnRadius.full)`.
- `CairnRadiusScale scaled(double radius)` — Recomputes the whole scale for a custom base radius. ```dart // A tighter theme built on a 6px base. CairnRadius.scaled(6).md; // 4.8 ```

## `CairnRadiusScale`

A radius scale derived from a custom base radius.

Produced by [CairnRadius.scaled]. Applies the same multipliers as the
default scale, so a retuned theme keeps proportional radii across every
component.

**Constructor** `CairnRadiusScale(double base)`

Creates a scale from a base radius in logical pixels.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `base` | `double` | yes |  | The base radius, in logical pixels. |

**Members**

- `double get sm` — `base * 0.6`.
- `double get md` — `base * 0.8`.
- `double get lg` — `base`.
- `double get xl` — `base * 1.4`.
- `double get xl2` — `base * 1.8`.
- `double get xl3` — `base * 2.2`.
- `double get xl4` — `base * 2.6`.

## `CairnShadows`

Tailwind CSS's box-shadow scale, translated to Flutter [BoxShadow] lists.

## Why this is not a direct field-for-field copy

CSS and Flutter disagree about what "blur radius" means, so copying the
numbers out of `box-shadow` straight into [BoxShadow.blurRadius] produces a
visibly softer, larger shadow than the browser draws.

* **CSS** specifies that a shadow's blur is a Gaussian whose *standard
  deviation is half the blur-radius value*. So `0 1px 3px` means sigma 1.5.
* **Flutter** converts [BoxShadow.blurRadius] to a sigma with
  `sigma = radius * 0.57735 + 0.5` (`BoxShadow.blurSigma`, inherited from
  Skia's `convertRadiusToSigma`).

Setting `blurRadius: 3` in Flutter therefore yields sigma `2.23`, roughly
50% wider than the browser's `1.5`. [cssBlur] inverts Flutter's formula so
the rendered sigma matches the CSS one:

```text
blurRadius = (cssBlurPx / 2 - 0.5) / 0.57735
```

CSS's fourth `box-shadow` length — spread — maps cleanly onto
[BoxShadow.spreadRadius], including the negative spreads Tailwind uses to
keep large shadows tight against their element.

**Static members**

- `List<BoxShadow> none = <BoxShadow>[]` — `shadow-none`.
- `double cssBlur(double cssBlurPx)` — Converts a CSS blur-radius in px to the [BoxShadow.blurRadius] that makes Flutter render the same Gaussian sigma a browser would. Returns 0 for CSS blurs of 1px or less, where the inverted formula would go negative — such shadows are effectively hard edges in both engines.
- `List<BoxShadow> xs2` — `shadow-2xs` — `0 1px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.05)`.
- `List<BoxShadow> xs` — `shadow-xs` — `0 1px 2px 0 rgb(0 0 0 / 0.05)`. The default resting elevation for Input, Textarea, Select trigger, Checkbox, Switch and the outline Button variant.
- `List<BoxShadow> sm` — `shadow-sm` — `0 1px 3px 0 rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1), 0 1px 2px -1px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1)`. Used by Card and the active Tabs trigger.
- `List<BoxShadow> md` — `shadow-md` — `0 4px 6px -1px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1), 0 2px 4px -2px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1)`. Used by Popover, Dropdown Menu, Select and Hover Card content.
- `List<BoxShadow> lg` — `shadow-lg` — `0 10px 15px -3px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1), 0 4px 6px -4px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1)`. Used by Dialog, Alert Dialog, Sheet and submenu content.
- `List<BoxShadow> xl` — `shadow-xl` — `0 20px 25px -5px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1), 0 8px 10px -6px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1)`.
- `List<BoxShadow> xl2` — `shadow-2xl` — `0 25px 50px -12px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.25)`.

## `CairnSpacing`

Tailwind CSS's spacing scale, expressed in Flutter logical pixels.

Tailwind v4 defines a single spacing base — `--spacing: 0.25rem` — and every
numeric spacing utility is a multiple of it. With the browser default root
font size of 16px, `0.25rem` is 4px, so `p-4` is `4 * 4px = 16px`.

Flutter's logical pixel is the same unit as a CSS px at `devicePixelRatio`
1, so the conversion is 1:1 with no scaling factor.

```text
Tailwind class   rem      css px   CairnSpacing
gap-1            0.25rem  4px      CairnSpacing.s1
px-3             0.75rem  12px     CairnSpacing.s3
p-6              1.5rem   24px     CairnSpacing.s6
```

**Static members**

- `double base = 4.0` — The Tailwind spacing base, `--spacing: 0.25rem` = 4 logical pixels. Prefer the named steps below; use this directly only when translating a class Tailwind expresses as a raw multiple of `--spacing`.
- `double s0 = 0.0` — `0` — zero spacing.
- `double s0p5 = 2.0` — `0.5` — 0.125rem / 2px.
- `double s1 = 4.0` — `1` — 0.25rem / 4px.
- `double s1p5 = 6.0` — `1.5` — 0.375rem / 6px.
- `double s2 = 8.0` — `2` — 0.5rem / 8px.
- `double s2p5 = 10.0` — `2.5` — 0.625rem / 10px.
- `double s3 = 12.0` — `3` — 0.75rem / 12px.
- `double s3p5 = 14.0` — `3.5` — 0.875rem / 14px.
- `double s4 = 16.0` — `4` — 1rem / 16px.
- `double s5 = 20.0` — `5` — 1.25rem / 20px.
- `double s6 = 24.0` — `6` — 1.5rem / 24px.
- `double s7 = 28.0` — `7` — 1.75rem / 28px.
- `double s8 = 32.0` — `8` — 2rem / 32px.
- `double s9 = 36.0` — `9` — 2.25rem / 36px.
- `double s10 = 40.0` — `10` — 2.5rem / 40px.
- `double s11 = 44.0` — `11` — 2.75rem / 44px.
- `double s12 = 48.0` — `12` — 3rem / 48px.
- `double s16 = 64.0` — `16` — 4rem / 64px.
- `double s20 = 80.0` — `20` — 5rem / 80px.
- `double s24 = 96.0` — `24` — 6rem / 96px.
- `double step(double multiplier)` — Resolves an arbitrary Tailwind spacing step to logical pixels. `CairnSpacing.step(3.5)` is `14.0`, matching `p-3.5`.

## `CairnTone`

A semantic intent a component can be tinted with. Components that communicate *state* — a Status dot, a Steps indicator, a
Timeline marker — need a few more intents than that, so Cairn adds three
(`success`, `warning`, `info`) as an extension of the token layer rather
than as colours hardcoded into each component.

## `CairnToneColor`

A fill and the foreground that belongs on it.

**Constructor** `CairnToneColor(Color fill, Color onFill)`

Creates a fill/foreground pair.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `fill` | `Color` | yes |  | The solid colour for dots, markers and filled shapes. |
| `onFill` | `Color` | yes |  | The colour for text and icons placed on [fill]. |

## `CairnToneColors`

Resolves a [CairnTone] to concrete colours for a [CairnTheme].

Like every other Cairn colour, the additions are authored in OKLCH and
converted by the package, so their provenance is checkable. The light
values sit at Tailwind's 600 step (500 for warning, which needs the extra
lightness to read as amber rather than brown) and the dark values at the
400 step, mirroring how `destructive` is lifted in the dark theme.

**Static members**

- `CairnToneColor resolve(CairnTheme theme, CairnTone tone)` — The colours for [tone] under [theme].

## `CairnTypography`

Tailwind CSS's type scale, expressed as Flutter [TextStyle]s.

## Font size and line height

Tailwind's `text-*` utilities set a font size *and* a paired line height.
Both are authored in `rem`, which resolves against the 16px browser root
font size, so `text-sm` is `0.875rem / 1.25rem` = 14px text on a 20px line.

Flutter expresses line height as [TextStyle.height], a **multiple of the
font size**, not an absolute length. The conversion is therefore:

```text
height = cssLineHeightPx / cssFontSizePx
text-sm -> 20 / 14 = 1.4285714...
```

Baking the ratio rather than the pixel value is what keeps a component's
intrinsic height correct when a user scales text.

## Tight leading

A few places in the library — Card title, Dialog title, Label — want a line
height of exactly 1, so that a single-line heading occupies precisely its
own font size and sits optically centred against the controls beside it.
Flutter's default when [height] is null is *not* 1: it is the font's own
metric ascent+descent, typically ~1.2, which drops the glyphs low in their
box. [leadingNone] exists for exactly that case and has to be set
explicitly.

## Font family

Cairn never names a typeface. [CairnTypography] leaves
[TextStyle.fontFamily] null so the ambient font the host app configures
applies throughout, which is what lets Cairn drop into an existing app
without fighting its brand. The golden tests pin a bundled font instead, so
rendering stays deterministic in CI. See `README.md` for the golden-font
setup.

**Static members**

- `TextStyle xs = TextStyle(fontSize: 12.0, height: 16.0 / 12.0, fontWeight: normal)` — `text-xs` — 0.75rem / 1rem (12px on a 16px line). Badge, Kbd, Tooltip content, menu shortcuts and Select group labels.
- `TextStyle sm = TextStyle(fontSize: 14.0, height: 20.0 / 14.0, fontWeight: normal)` — `text-sm` — 0.875rem / 1.25rem (14px on a 20px line). The library's workhorse size: Button, Input, Label, menu items, Table.
- `TextStyle base = TextStyle(fontSize: 16.0, height: 24.0 / 16.0, fontWeight: normal)` — `text-base` — 1rem / 1.5rem (16px on a 24px line).
- `TextStyle lg = TextStyle(fontSize: 18.0, height: 28.0 / 18.0, fontWeight: normal)` — `text-lg` — 1.125rem / 1.75rem (18px on a 28px line). Dialog and Alert Dialog titles.
- `TextStyle xl = TextStyle(fontSize: 20.0, height: 28.0 / 20.0, fontWeight: normal)` — `text-xl` — 1.25rem / 1.75rem (20px on a 28px line).
- `TextStyle xl2 = TextStyle(fontSize: 24.0, height: 32.0 / 24.0, fontWeight: normal)` — `text-2xl` — 1.5rem / 2rem (24px on a 32px line).
- `TextStyle xl3 = TextStyle(fontSize: 30.0, height: 36.0 / 30.0, fontWeight: normal)` — `text-3xl` — 1.875rem / 2.25rem (30px on a 36px line).
- `TextStyle xl4 = TextStyle(fontSize: 36.0, height: 40.0 / 36.0, fontWeight: normal)` — `text-4xl` — 2.25rem / 2.5rem (36px on a 40px line).
- `FontWeight normal = FontWeight.w400` — `font-normal` — CSS weight 400.
- `FontWeight medium = FontWeight.w500` — `font-medium` — CSS weight 500. Button labels, Label, Alert titles, menu group labels.
- `FontWeight semibold = FontWeight.w600` — `font-semibold` — CSS weight 600. Card, Dialog and Sheet titles.
- `FontWeight bold = FontWeight.w700` — `font-bold` — CSS weight 700.
- `double leadingNone = 1.0` — `leading-none` — `line-height: 1`. Must be applied explicitly; Flutter's default line height comes from font metrics (~1.2), not 1.0.
- `double leadingRelaxed = 1.625` — `leading-relaxed` — `line-height: 1.625`.
- `double trackingTight(double fontSize)` — `tracking-tight` — `letter-spacing: -0.025em`. Returns an absolute value in logical pixels, because Flutter's [TextStyle.letterSpacing] is absolute where CSS's `em` is relative.
- `double trackingWidest(double fontSize)` — `tracking-widest` — `letter-spacing: 0.1em`. Used by menu shortcuts.


---

# Introduction

Cairn is a modern, accessible component library for Flutter, built on one design-token layer: spacing, radii, OKLCH colour, a type scale, shadows and a focus-ring treatment, all specified once and held in place by golden tests.

### What this is

Sixty-five components, no runtime dependencies beyond Flutter itself, and a token layer where every value records the source string it was converted from. It is a widget package: no backend, no network layer, no platform channels, no native code.

The site you are reading is built with it. The navigation bar, the search trigger, the code block copy buttons, the preview/code tabs, the mobile navigation sheet and the command palette behind Ctrl+K are all Cairn widgets doing a real job, not demonstrations sitting in a grid. If a component regresses upstream, this site breaks.


### What "token-driven" means here

Plenty of libraries describe themselves as token-driven and still hardcode a 13 somewhere inside a widget. Cairn treats that as a bug, and the claim it makes is narrow enough to be checkable:

1. No component hardcodes a value that belongs in a token file. Padding, height, gap, radius, font size, shadow, ring width and transition all resolve to a named token.
2. Every conversion between CSS semantics and Flutter semantics is explicit and documented where the two disagree — of which there are more than you would expect.
3. Golden tests lock the rendered result down, so the implementation cannot drift once it is right.


### How the values are specified

The design system is written in CSS terms — the notation this kind of system is normally expressed in — and converted into Flutter once, in the token layer, rather than ad hoc at each call site.

| Written as | Becomes |
| --- | --- |
| Tailwind-style utility strings (h-9, px-4, gap-2, text-sm) | Per-component padding, height, gap, font size, shadow, ring and transition constants |
| oklch() custom properties, light and dark | The nineteen semantic colour slots plus the five-step chart ramp |
| A multiplier formula over a single --radius base | The rounded-* radius scale, rescalable from one number |
| Tailwind CSS v4's published scales | The 0.25rem spacing base, the type scale and the box-shadow values |

Each token file records the source string next to the converted value, so the provenance of any number is one click away in the source:

`lib/src/tokens/colors.dart`
```dart
/// `--primary: oklch(0.205 0 0)` — `#171717` (neutral-900).
static const Color lightPrimary = Color(0xFF171717);
```


### Four conversions that are easy to get wrong

CSS and Flutter agree on far less than they appear to. These are the four places where a literal reading of a value produces something visibly wrong, and they are the reason the conversions live in one documented layer rather than being repeated per component:

- Colour is defined in OKLCH, not HSL. OKLCH is perceptually uniform, so a lightness step means the same thing at every hue — which is what makes an achromatic ramp stay neutral. Anything that round-trips the palette through HSL loses that.
- The radius scale is multiplier-based, not offset-based. Every step is --radius × a factor (0.6, 0.8, 1.0, 1.4, 1.8), so setting one number rescales a whole app proportionally. Fixed ± 4px offsets agree at the default and diverge the moment --radius is customised.
- A CSS blur radius is not a Flutter blur radius. CSS treats it as twice the Gaussian sigma; Flutter feeds it through Skia's radius × 0.57735 + 0.5. Pasting the number across draws a shadow roughly 50% too wide.
- An opacity modifier scales alpha, it does not set it. A token that already carries 15% alpha, taken to /30, lands at 4.5% — not 30%. Six times too strong is very visible on a dark-mode form control.

> **A correctness check fell out of the conversion** Every achromatic step lands exactly on Tailwind's published neutral hex ramp — oklch(0.145 0 0) → #0A0A0A = neutral-950, oklch(0.922 0 0) → #E5E5E5 = neutral-200, and so on. test/tokens/tokens_test.dart asserts this, which means a bug in the OKLCH → sRGB pipeline could not pass CI unnoticed.


### What it deliberately does not do

Cairn does not ship a form-validation engine — Flutter has Form and FormField, and competing with them would fight the framework. It does not ship a theme-builder UI, and it does not ship icon assets: the handful of glyphs components need are drawn from Lucide's geometry with a CustomPainter, so the package stays pure Dart.

---

# Installation

Cairn is a normal Flutter package with no transitive dependencies. Add it, import one barrel, and register the theme extension.

### Add the dependency

From pub.dev, once published:

`pubspec.yaml`
```yaml
dependencies:
  cairn_ui: ^0.2.0
```

Or straight from git. Pin an exact commit rather than a branch — a floating ref means an upstream push can change what your app renders between two builds of the same source, which turns a visual regression into a mystery:

`pubspec.yaml`
```yaml
dependencies:
  cairn_ui:
    git:
      url: https://github.com/rlphjyson/cairn_ui.git
      ref: v0.2.0
```

```shell
flutter pub get
```


### Import

One barrel exports every component, token and theme type. There are no per-component imports to remember.

```dart
import 'package:cairn_ui/cairn_ui.dart';
```


### Register the theme

CairnTheme is a ThemeExtension, so it rides on ThemeData rather than introducing a second theme system. CairnTheme.materialTheme() builds a ThemeData whose Material defaults already agree with the Cairn tokens:

```dart
MaterialApp(
  theme: CairnTheme.materialTheme(CairnTheme.light),
  darkTheme: CairnTheme.materialTheme(CairnTheme.dark),
  themeMode: ThemeMode.dark,
  home: const HomeScreen(),
)
```

> **Components never throw for a missing theme** CairnTheme.of(context) falls back to CairnTheme.light rather than asserting, so a Cairn widget dropped into an app that never registered the extension still renders with correct tokens. Register the extension to control which theme is used, not to make things work at all.


### Fonts

Cairn's typography tokens leave fontFamily null — the type scale is about size, line height, weight and tracking, not about which typeface you use. Whatever your app sets is inherited. To use the font this site and the golden tests use, bundle Geist and set it once on the theme:

```dart
CairnTheme.materialTheme(
  CairnTheme.dark.copyWith(fontFamily: 'Geist'),
)
```

That is precisely what this site does — Geist is bundled under fonts/, registered in pubspec.yaml, and applied with a single copyWith at the theme root.


### Platform support

There is nothing platform-specific to break: no platform channels, no native code, no plugins. The package declares every target Flutter supports. This site is the Flutter web build.

---

# Quick start

A complete, runnable app in about thirty lines, and the three patterns you will use constantly.

### A complete app

`lib/main.dart`
```dart
import 'package:cairn_ui/cairn_ui.dart';
import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

void main() => runApp(const MyApp());

class MyApp extends StatelessWidget {
  const MyApp({super.key});

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return MaterialApp(
      theme: CairnTheme.materialTheme(CairnTheme.light),
      darkTheme: CairnTheme.materialTheme(CairnTheme.dark),
      themeMode: ThemeMode.dark,
      // The toast host sits above every route, so a toast outlives the
      // screen that fired it.
      builder: (BuildContext context, Widget? child) =>
          CairnToaster(child: child ?? const SizedBox.shrink()),
      home: Scaffold(
        body: Center(
          child: CairnCard(
            width: 360,
            children: <Widget>[
              const CairnCardHeader(
                title: Text('Deploy your project'),
                description: Text('Ship to production in one click.'),
              ),
              CairnCardFooter(
                mainAxisAlignment: MainAxisAlignment.end,
                children: <Widget>[
                  CairnButton(
                    variant: CairnButtonVariant.outline,
                    onPressed: () {},
                    child: const Text('Cancel'),
                  ),
                  CairnButton(onPressed: () {}, child: const Text('Deploy')),
                ],
              ),
            ],
          ),
        ),
      ),
    );
  }
}
```


### Reading tokens

Anywhere you need a colour, a radius or a type style in your own widgets, read it from the theme rather than hardcoding it. This is how everything on this site is built:

```dart
final CairnTheme theme = CairnTheme.of(context);

Container(
  padding: const EdgeInsets.all(CairnSpacing.s4),
  decoration: BoxDecoration(
    color: theme.card,
    border: Border.all(color: theme.border),
    borderRadius: BorderRadius.circular(theme.radiusScale.lg),
  ),
  child: Text(
    'Custom surface, Cairn tokens',
    style: theme
        .textStyle(CairnTypography.sm)
        .copyWith(color: theme.mutedForeground),
  ),
)
```

> **Use theme.radiusScale, not CairnRadius, in app code** CairnRadius.lg is the constant for the default --radius of 10px. theme.radiusScale.lg re-derives it from whatever --radius the active theme carries, so a themed app with a tighter radius keeps your own surfaces proportional instead of leaving them at 10.


### Overlays

Modal surfaces — Dialog, Alert Dialog, Sheet, Drawer — are opened with a show* function that pushes a PopupRoute, which is what gives you focus trapping, focus restore and back-gesture dismissal for free:

```dart
await showCairnDialog<void>(
  context: context,
  builder: (BuildContext context) => CairnDialog(
    title: const Text('Edit profile'),
    content: const CairnFormField(label: 'Name', child: CairnInput()),
    actions: <Widget>[
      CairnButton(onPressed: () => Navigator.pop(context), child: const Text('Save')),
    ],
  ),
);
```

Anchored surfaces — Popover, Dropdown Menu, Tooltip, Hover Card — use OverlayPortal instead, so they stay out of the navigation stack. Those take a CairnOverlayController you own:

```dart
final CairnOverlayController controller = CairnOverlayController();

@override
void dispose() {
  controller.dispose();
  super.dispose();
}

CairnPopover(
  controller: controller,
  content: const CairnPopoverTitle('Dimensions'),
  child: CairnButton(
    onPressed: controller.toggle,
    child: const Text('Open'),
  ),
)
```


### Toasts

Install CairnToaster once in MaterialApp.builder, above the Navigator. Then any widget can fire a toast and it will survive that widget's route being popped.

```dart
CairnToast.show(
  context,
  const CairnToast(
    variant: CairnToastVariant.success,
    title: 'Changes saved',
    description: 'Your profile is up to date.',
  ),
);
```

---

# Theming

CairnTheme is a ThemeExtension carrying nineteen semantic colour slots, a radius base and a font family. Everything else is derived.

### Why a ThemeExtension

This is a deliberate integration choice, not a shortcut. An inherited widget of Cairn's own would force host apps to nest two theme systems and would break any Material widget already in use. Riding on ThemeData.extensions instead means three things:

- Cairn composes inside an ordinary MaterialApp; nothing has to be abandoned or wrapped.
- Flutter animates theme changes for free, because ThemeExtension.lerp is driven by AnimatedTheme during a light/dark transition — the toggle in this site's header is a plain setState, and the crossfade you see is Flutter interpolating every token.
- Theme.of(context) stays the single lookup path developers already know.

```dart
MaterialApp(
  theme: CairnTheme.materialTheme(CairnTheme.light),
  darkTheme: CairnTheme.materialTheme(CairnTheme.dark),
)
```

materialTheme() also aligns Material's own defaults with the Cairn tokens: scaffold and canvas colours, a matching ColorScheme, text selection colours, no ink splash — Cairn's interactions are colour and shadow transitions, not ripples — and Material 3's filled TextField default switched off, since Cairn inputs are transparent-backed with a border.

If you would rather wire it yourself:

```dart
MaterialApp(
  theme: ThemeData(
    extensions: const <ThemeExtension<dynamic>>[CairnTheme.light],
  ),
)
```


### The colour slots

Nineteen semantic slots, each named for the CSS custom property it is specified as. They come in background/foreground pairs so that a surface and the text on it always move together.

| Slot | CSS variable | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| background / foreground | --background | The page surface and default body text |
| card / cardForeground | --card | Raised content surfaces |
| popover / popoverForeground | --popover | Floating surfaces: Popover, Dropdown, Select, Tooltip, Command |
| primary / primaryForeground | --primary | High-emphasis fills: default Button, checked Checkbox and Switch, Progress |
| secondary / secondaryForeground | --secondary | Low-emphasis fills: secondary Button and Badge |
| muted / mutedForeground | --muted | De-emphasised backgrounds and secondary text |
| accent / accentForeground | --accent | Hover and keyboard-focus highlight for interactive rows |
| destructive / destructiveForeground | --destructive | Danger fills and destructive text |
| border | --border | Hairlines and component outlines |
| input | --input | The border colour of form controls specifically |
| ring | --ring | The focus ring, drawn at 50% alpha and 3px |

> **destructiveForeground is a real slot, not a hardcoded white** The common convention is to paint white text onto a destructive fill and leave it at that, which stops working the moment someone themes destructive to a pale colour. Cairn keeps the foreground as its own themeable slot and merely defaults it to white.


### Tones

The palette stops at primary, secondary and destructive, which is not enough for components that carry state. CairnTone adds the missing ones: an enum of neutral, primary, success, warning, info and destructive, resolved against the active theme by CairnToneColors.resolve into a fill and the foreground that belongs on it.

| Tone | Light | Dark |
| --- | --- | --- |
| success | green-600 | green-400 |
| warning | amber-500 | amber-400 |
| info | blue-600 | blue-400 |

Like every other Cairn colour, the additions are authored in OKLCH with separate light and dark values. Status, Steps, Timeline, Rating and Radial Progress all take a tone.

```dart
final CairnToneColor c = CairnToneColors.resolve(
  CairnTheme.of(context),
  CairnTone.success,
);
// c.fill for dots and markers, c.onFill for text placed on it
```


### The radius scale

One base, --radius, defaults to 0.625rem = 10 logical pixels. Every other step is a multiplier of it rather than a fixed offset from it, which is what lets a single number rescale an entire app:

| Step | Formula | Default | Used by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| xs | fixed 2px | 2 | Dialog and Sheet close affordances |
| sm | --radius × 0.6 | 6 | Badge, small chips |
| md | --radius × 0.8 | 8 | Button, Input, Textarea, Select, Popover, Dropdown |
| lg | --radius | 10 | Dialog, Alert, Tabs list |
| xl | --radius × 1.4 | 14 | Card |
| 2xl | --radius × 1.8 | 18 |  |
| full | 9999 | pill | Avatar, Switch, Pagination |

Change radius on the theme and every component's corners rescale proportionally. Read theme.radiusScale in your own widgets so they rescale too.

```dart
final CairnTheme tight = CairnTheme.dark.copyWith(radius: 4.0);
// tight.radiusScale.md == 3.2, tight.radiusScale.xl == 5.6
```


### Customising

copyWith on either preset. Nothing else is needed — there is no builder, no config file and no code generation.

```dart
final CairnTheme brand = CairnTheme.light.copyWith(
  primary: const Color(0xFF3B82F6),
  primaryForeground: const Color(0xFFFFFFFF),
  radius: 4.0,
  fontFamily: 'Inter',
);

MaterialApp(theme: CairnTheme.materialTheme(brand));
```


### Derived values

A few things are computed from the slots rather than stored, so they cannot drift out of sync:

| Getter | What it returns |
| --- | --- |
| ringMuted | ring at 50% alpha — Tailwind's ring-ring/50 |
| focusRing | The ring as a BoxShadow list: zero offset, zero blur, 3px spread, because Tailwind compiles ring-[3px] to box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px |
| invalidRing | The ring tinted destructive, at 20% in light and 40% in dark |
| radiusScale | The derived rounded-* scale for this theme's radius |
| defaultTextStyle | text-sm in foreground |


### The opacity modifier trap

Tailwind's /N modifier scales a colour's existing alpha; it does not set it. bg-input/30 compiles to color-mix(in oklab, var(--input) 30%, transparent). For an opaque token that is the same as setting alpha to 0.30 — but Cairn's dark --input is already oklch(1 0 0 / 15%), so dark:bg-input/30 is white at 4.5%, not 30%. Six times too strong is very visible as a washed-out grey fill on every dark-mode form control.

```dart
// The extension Cairn ships for exactly this.
extension CairnOpacityModifier on Color {
  Color withOpacityModifier(double factor) =>
      withValues(alpha: a * factor.clamp(0.0, 1.0));
}

theme.input.withOpacityModifier(0.3); // scales, does not replace
```

---

# Design tokens

Seven token files, each recording where its numbers came from. No component hardcodes a value that should come from one of these.

### The files

| File | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| tokens/oklch.dart | oklch() → Color conversion, following Björn Ottosson's OKLab specification |
| tokens/colors.dart | All 19 semantic slots plus the 5-step chart ramp, light and dark, each annotated with its source oklch() string |
| tokens/spacing.dart | Tailwind's 0.25rem scale |
| tokens/radius.dart | The --radius scale and CairnRadiusScale for custom bases |
| tokens/typography.dart | Font sizes, line-height ratios, weights, tracking |
| tokens/shadows.dart | The shadow scale plus the CSS-blur conversion |
| tokens/motion.dart | Durations and Tailwind's easing curves |


### Spacing

Tailwind v4 defines a single base — --spacing: 0.25rem — and every numeric spacing utility is a multiple of it. At the browser default 16px root, that is 4px, and a Flutter logical pixel is the same unit as a CSS px at devicePixelRatio 1. The conversion is 1:1 with no scaling factor.

```dart
CairnSpacing.s1;   //  4 — gap-1
CairnSpacing.s3;   // 12 — px-3
CairnSpacing.s6;   // 24 — p-6
CairnSpacing.step(3.5); // 14 — p-3.5
```


### Typography

Tailwind pairs a font size with an absolute line height: text-sm is 0.875rem / 1.25rem. Flutter's TextStyle.height is a multiple of the font size, not a length, so the conversion is 20 / 14 = 1.4286. Baking the ratio rather than the pixel value is what keeps a component's intrinsic height correct when a user scales text.

> **leading-none is not Flutter's default** Card, Dialog and Label titles use line-height: 1. Flutter's default when height is null comes from the font's own metrics, typically around 1.2, so these have to set height: 1.0 explicitly or titles sit visibly low in their box.

```dart
CairnTypography.sm;       // 14px on a 20px line
CairnTypography.xl2;      // 24px on a 32px line
CairnTypography.semibold; // FontWeight.w600
CairnTypography.leadingNone;          // 1.0
CairnTypography.trackingTight(24);    // -0.6, because em is relative
```


### Shadows and the blur conversion

This is the conversion that is wrong if you copy the numbers across literally. CSS defines a shadow's blur as a Gaussian whose standard deviation is half the stated radius, so 0 1px 3px means sigma 1.5. Flutter converts BoxShadow.blurRadius to a sigma with radius × 0.57735 + 0.5, inherited from Skia's convertRadiusToSigma. Pasting CSS's 3 into blurRadius yields sigma 2.23 — roughly 50% wider than the browser draws.

```dart
// Inverts Flutter's formula so the rendered sigma matches CSS's.
static double cssBlur(double cssBlurPx) {
  final double targetSigma = cssBlurPx / 2.0;
  if (targetSigma <= 0.5) return 0.0;
  return (targetSigma - 0.5) / 0.57735;
}
```

> **Outer shadows are clipped in CSS and not in Flutter** CSS never paints an outer box-shadow through its element; Flutter paints a blurred filled copy of the shape behind the box with no clip. On Cairn's transparent-backed form controls that turns shadow-xs into a grey wash across the field — and turns focus-visible:ring-[3px], which compiles to box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px, into a solid fill over the entire control instead of a 3px outline. CairnShadowed paints shadows through a clip that removes the shape's interior.


### Motion

Tailwind's transition utilities default to 150ms with cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1) — the curve Tailwind calls ease-in-out, which is not the CSS keyword ease-in-out (that is 0.42, 0, 0.58, 1). Flutter has no built-in Curve for it, so CairnMotion.standard constructs it with the exact control points.

```dart
CairnMotion.d150;     // Tailwind's transition default
CairnMotion.d200;     // Dialog, Accordion, Popover
CairnMotion.d500;     // Sheet and Drawer opening (closing is d300)
CairnMotion.standard; // Cubic(0.4, 0.0, 0.2, 1.0)
CairnMotion.easeOut;  // Cubic(0.0, 0.0, 0.2, 1.0)
```

The hover lift on this site's cards, the theme toggle's icon rotation and the preview/code crossfade all read their duration and curve from these constants rather than picking numbers.


### The chart ramp

colors.dart also carries --chart-1 through --chart-5. In the Neutral base these are achromatic — #D4D4D4 through #262626 — which is why the Charts page on this site is monochrome by default rather than reaching for a palette Cairn does not define.

---

# Dark mode

Both themes ship. Switching between them is one field on MaterialApp, and Flutter animates every token across the change.

### The two presets

CairnTheme.light and CairnTheme.dark are Cairn's Neutral base — an achromatic palette specified in OKLCH, where every step lands exactly on a published neutral ramp. Hand both to MaterialApp and pick with themeMode:

```dart
MaterialApp(
  theme: CairnTheme.materialTheme(CairnTheme.light),
  darkTheme: CairnTheme.materialTheme(CairnTheme.dark),
  themeMode: _mode, // ThemeMode.dark, .light or .system
)
```


### How this site does it

The toggle in the header is a ChangeNotifier holding a ThemeMode, exposed through an InheritedNotifier. It defaults to ThemeMode.dark rather than ThemeMode.system, and it only ever moves between the two explicit modes — so a visitor whose OS is already dark still sees the control do something.

`lib/src/app/site_theme.dart`
```dart
class SiteThemeController extends ChangeNotifier {
  SiteThemeController({ThemeMode initial = ThemeMode.dark}) : _mode = initial;

  ThemeMode _mode;
  ThemeMode get mode => _mode;
  bool get isDark => _mode == ThemeMode.dark;

  void toggle() {
    _mode = _mode == ThemeMode.dark ? ThemeMode.light : ThemeMode.dark;
    notifyListeners();
  }
}
```

There is one escape hatch: appending ?theme=light to any URL on this site boots into the light theme. That is not a preference store — it exists so a light-mode screenshot can be captured head-lessly and so a link can point at a specific treatment. Anyone who simply opens the site still gets dark.

> **The crossfade is free** CairnTheme implements ThemeExtension.lerp, interpolating every colour slot and the radius. MaterialApp wraps its child in an AnimatedTheme, so flipping themeMode animates all nineteen slots over Flutter's default theme duration. There is no explicit animation anywhere in this site's toggle code.


### Where dark is not just inverted light

A handful of components genuinely branch on brightness rather than on a token, because the design calls for a dark-only treatment with no light counterpart. The outline Button gains a subtle fill in dark mode that simply does not exist in light mode; the invalid focus ring goes from 20% to 40% alpha, because a destructive tint that reads clearly on white disappears on near-black. CairnTheme carries brightness precisely so those branches can be honest about it.

The dark theme also switches borders from an opaque grey to a translucent white — --border is oklch(1 0 0 / 10%) — so that a hairline lifts correctly over both the page background and a raised card. That is why theme.border is not a flat colour you can blend against a known background.

---

# Accessibility

Looking right is the easy half. Focus, keyboard operation and screen-reader semantics are part of each component's contract in Cairn, not a pass somebody makes later.

### Focus-visible, not focus

Cairn draws its focus ring on focus-visible rather than focus: clicking a button must not show a ring, while tabbing to it must. Flutter's hasFocus cannot distinguish the two. CairnInteractive combines focus state with FocusManager.highlightMode and tracks whether the focus change came from a pointer press.

> **Try it** Click the button below — no ring. Then press Tab to move focus to it — a 3px ring at 50% alpha appears. That distinction is the difference between a focus indicator that helps keyboard users and one that looks like a rendering bug to mouse users.


### Keyboard

- Space and Enter both activate, wired through ActivateIntent so it composes with a host app's own shortcuts.
- Roving focus in Radio Group and Tabs: one tab stop for the group, arrow keys to move within it.
- Slider supports arrow keys plus Home and End, and exposes increase/decrease actions with correct increasedValue and decreasedValue announcements.
- Escape dismisses every overlay — except Alert Dialog, which by design demands an explicit choice.
- The Command palette keeps focus in its input while arrow keys move a highlight through the list, so typing and navigating never compete for the same keystrokes.


### Focus trapping and restore

Dialog, Alert Dialog, Sheet and Drawer push a PopupRoute, which gets Flutter's per-route FocusScope — so focus is trapped while they are open and restored to the trigger when they close. It also brings back-gesture dismissal, which a web implementation has no equivalent of. Anchored surfaces (Popover, Dropdown Menu) use OverlayPortal instead, so they stay out of the navigation stack and the system back gesture does not close them.


### Pointer events and disabled state

disabled:pointer-events-none genuinely removes the subtree from hit testing rather than just making the component itself inert. A disabled button with a tooltip wrapped around it will not show the tooltip, which is the correct web behaviour and is easy to get wrong in Flutter.


### Reduced motion

Skeleton, Spinner and the Input OTP caret honour MediaQuery.disableAnimations. That is also what makes golden tests possible: those components never stop scheduling frames, so the golden harness sets disableAnimations and captures one deterministic frame instead of timing out in pumpAndSettle.


### Semantics

Controls that have no visible label take a semanticLabel: icon buttons require one, and Switch, Slider, Progress and Avatar all accept one. Separator is decorative by default so screen readers skip it; pass decorative: false when the rule carries meaning. Breadcrumb announces its current crumb as the current page rather than rendering a dead link.

---

# Testing

Token extraction makes the first implementation correct. Golden tests are what keep it correct.

### What is tested

| Directory | What it covers |
| --- | --- |
| test/tokens/ | The OKLCH pipeline, the neutral-ramp assertion, the radius formula |
| test/components/ | Behaviour: focus, keyboard, dismissal, sizing |
| test/goldens/ | Every component as a variant sheet, in both themes |

```shell
flutter test                 # 114 tests
flutter analyze --fatal-infos --fatal-warnings
dart format --set-exit-if-changed .
```


### Why goldens are reliable here

Two decisions make golden comparison a signal rather than a source of flakes.

Fonts are bundled, not borrowed from the OS. flutter test loads no real font by default — text lays out with a placeholder where every glyph is an identical box, which tells you nothing about typography. Cairn ships Geist under test/fonts/ and registers it in test/flutter_test_config.dart, so text shapes identically everywhere.

Goldens are generated and verified on one platform. Even with identical fonts, sub-pixel anti-aliasing differs between operating systems. Rather than weaken the comparison with a fuzzy threshold — which would let real regressions through — Cairn enforces goldens on Linux, which is what CI runs. On Windows and macOS the widgets are still built and pumped, so layout errors and exceptions are caught, but the pixel comparison is skipped.

> **Regenerating goldens** Because references must come from the same platform that verifies them, do not run --update-goldens locally on Windows or macOS. Use the "Update goldens" workflow in Actions instead; it re-runs flutter test afterwards to prove the regenerated images actually pass.


### A gotcha worth stealing

Golden capture pumps a fixed number of frames rather than calling pumpAndSettle. Components with repeating animations — Spinner, the Skeleton pulse, the Input OTP caret, indeterminate Progress — never stop scheduling frames, so pumpAndSettle times out. The harness also sets MediaQueryData.disableAnimations, which those components honour, so they render as one deterministic frame.


### This site's own tests

cairn_site does not repeat the library's golden rigour — it is a marketing site, not the design-system source of truth. What it does test is that every route renders without throwing, that the dark theme is what a fresh visitor gets, that the toggle actually reaches the light theme, and that the catalogues are internally consistent: no duplicate slugs, no component whose detail route would 404.
